title: Newton's Laws — Model Aircraft Motion in One Dimension
learningObjectives: Explain how inertia keeps velocity constant when net force is zero.
Relate net force and mass to acceleration using a=F_net/m.
Describe how balanced and unbalanced forces affect motion along a single direction.

explanations.text: When forces cancel, there is no net push to change motion, so velocity stays constant. Inertia describes the resistance to a change in motion.

evidence.quote: If all the external forces cancel each other out, then there is no net force acting on the object.
If there is no net force acting on the object, then the object will maintain a constant velocity.

explanations.text: Acceleration in one direction is produced by net force divided by mass. For constant mass, greater force gives greater acceleration and greater mass gives smaller acceleration for the same force.

evidence.quote: The acceleration of an object depends on the mass of the object and the amount of force applied.

explanations.text: Change in velocity over change in time defines acceleration, and the relationship can be used to predict how motion evolves when forces act along a straight line.

evidence.quote: The change in velocity divided by the change in time is the definition of the acceleration a.
This tendency to resist changes in a state of motion is inertia.
